characters.description: A young colonist who arrives on Pern with the Hanrahan family. Curious, adventurous, and unusually receptive to the planet's native creatures, Sorka grows up alongside the settlement and becomes one of the people most closely involved in its transformation.
characters.name: Sorka Hanrahan

characters.description: A boy from the Connell family, whose people bring experience with horses, herding, and a mobile way of life to the colony. Sean is independent, direct, and more comfortable proving himself through action than accepting authority on its own terms.
characters.name: Sean Connell

characters.description: The expedition's admiral and one of the senior leaders responsible for bringing the colonists safely to Pern. Paul supports the settlers' chartered plan for a permanent, largely agrarian society and must balance that ideal with the technical demands of establishing it.
characters.name: Paul Benden

characters.description: The colony's governor and Paul Benden's partner in civil leadership. Emily is calm, diplomatic, and attentive to the different groups that must become a functioning community after the expedition's ships have delivered them.
characters.name: Emily Boll

characters.description: An expert shuttle pilot who helps ferry people and equipment from the colony ships to the surface. Sallah is disciplined, courageous, and committed to the settlement, with the judgment to recognize when a flight requires more than technical skill.
characters.name: Sallah Telgar

characters.description: A talented engineer central to the colony's machinery, power, and transport systems. Tarvi understands that the settlers' decision to limit advanced technology still depends on using their inherited equipment wisely during the dangerous first years.
characters.name: Tarvi Andiyar

characters.description: One of the expedition's most accomplished pilots. Avril values the interstellar skills and technology the colonists intend to leave behind, and she is openly dissatisfied with a future confined to farming on an isolated world.
characters.name: Avril Bitra

characters.description: A senior geneticist whose knowledge is essential to adapting Earth plants and animals to their new environment. Kitti is authoritative, inventive, and prepared to use the colony's biological technology where it offers a durable answer to Pern's needs.
characters.name: Kitti Ping

characters.description: Kitti Ping's granddaughter and scientific assistant. Wind Blossom has inherited formidable technical ability, but she works under the expectations created by her grandmother's reputation and by the colony's urgent biological problems.
characters.name: Wind Blossom

characters.description: Sorka's father, an experienced horseman whose practical knowledge helps establish the colony's herds. Red is protective of his family and willing to judge unfamiliar Pernese life by close observation rather than fear.
characters.name: Red Hanrahan

characters.description: Sorka's mother and a capable member of the colony's farming community. Mairi combines family care with the work of settlement and helps give Sorka the security to explore the new world around Landing.
characters.name: Mairi Hanrahan

characters.description: A geneticist who works with Kitti Ping on the colony's biological program. Pol brings careful scientific knowledge to the adaptation of imported species and to the study of native Pernese life.
characters.name: Pol Nietro

characters.description: A colonist who distrusts the leadership's decisions and objects to the permanence of Pern's isolation. Ted is technically resourceful and persistent, but his determination to appeal beyond the colony places him in conflict with its agreed charter.
characters.name: Ted Tubberman

recaps.ending: The genetically created dragons prove able to bond permanently with human riders, fly, breathe flame after chewing firestone, and travel between places. Sorka and Faranth, Sean and Carenath, and the other first pairs turn Kitti Ping's experiment into a workable defense against Thread. Sean's authority among the riders grows from experience rather than appointment, while Sorka becomes the leading queen rider. The old colony at Landing can no longer remain the center of settlement, so people, animals, and salvageable equipment move north. The dragonriders take the great volcanic caverns above Fort as their home, creating the pattern later known as a Weyr. Avril Bitra's attempt to seize a way off Pern ends in space, and Sallah Telgar dies preventing her escape. The settlers lose much of their connection to advanced interstellar life, but they survive by combining what remains of that knowledge with dragons and new social institutions. Pern's later Holds, Weyrs, and founding legends begin in those choices.
recaps.in_short: Earth colonists arrive on Pern intending to build a permanent low-technology society at Landing. Children Sorka Hanrahan and Sean Connell grow up as the settlement prospers and form bonds with native fire-lizards. Years later, Thread begins falling without warning, consuming living matter and overwhelming the colony's limited aircraft and fuel. Geneticist Kitti Ping enlarges and reshapes fire-lizard embryos to create intelligent defenders. At the first hatching, Sorka bonds with the gold Faranth, Sean with bronze Carenath, and other young people become the first dragonriders. The dragons learn to fly, breathe flame using firestone, and move instantly between locations, giving Pern a renewable defense. Political division and Avril Bitra's attempted escape cost lives, including pilot Sallah Telgar's. Environmental danger and failing technology force the colonists to leave Landing and cross north. Sean, Sorka, and the riders settle in caverns above Fort, establishing the first Weyr and the institutions that will shape Pern after its origins become legend.

recaps.text: Three colony ships reach Pern with settlers who have deliberately chosen a permanent life away from Earth's crowded, technological civilization. Admiral Paul Benden and Governor Emily Boll oversee the descent to Landing, while pilots including Sallah Telgar and Avril Bitra ferry equipment and passengers to the surface. The Hanrahan and Connell families bring horses and practical husbandry alongside scientists, engineers, and farmers. Young Sorka Hanrahan explores eagerly and befriends Sean Connell. Native fire-lizards show unexpected intelligence and an ability to form intense bonds with people, suggesting that Pern's wildlife is stranger and more useful than the initial surveys revealed.

Landing develops into a successful settlement. Crops, herds, and outlying communities spread as the colonists use advanced equipment to establish the simpler society promised by their charter. Sorka and Sean grow toward adulthood, and their connection with fire-lizards deepens their understanding of the creatures' empathy and communication. Not everyone accepts the colony's direction: Avril resents the abandonment of interstellar life, while Ted Tubberman challenges the leadership's authority and looks for help beyond Pern. Even so, most settlers believe the hardest phase is behind them. The records warning of a periodic danger in the system have not yet become part of ordinary colonial planning.

Thread begins falling from the sky, its filaments devouring exposed plants, animals, and people wherever they touch ground. The first attacks devastate unprepared settlements and overturn every assumption about Pern's safety. Aircraft and chemical flamethrowers can destroy Thread in the air, but fuel, machines, and trained crews are finite. Paul, Emily, Tarvi, and the technical teams organize emergency flights and evacuations while trying to understand the Red Star's connection to the falls. The colony can survive individual attacks with its remaining technology, but it needs a defense that can reproduce and endure for generations.

The settlers map Thread's recurring falls and improvise wider defenses, yet every sortie consumes resources they cannot replace. Native fire-lizards can sense Thread and attack it, but they are too small to protect farms and settlements on their own. Kitti Ping proposes using the colony's genetic tools to enlarge and adapt the fire-lizard design into a powerful flying partner for humans. The project is controversial and urgent: the new creatures must remain intelligent and empathic while gaining the size, endurance, and firepower needed to fight Thread. Sorka, Sean, and other young people help tend the altered eggs as the colony waits to learn whether the experiment will produce protectors or another burden.

Kitti Ping's altered eggs hatch into dragons. Each hatchling chooses a human partner in an immediate mental bond: Sorka Impresses the golden Faranth, Sean the bronze Carenath, and the other young attendants form the first group of riders. The dragons grow rapidly, communicate with their riders, and begin learning the coordinated skills their task requires. Sean emerges as a practical leader because he understands both the animals and the independent people bonded to them. The experiment has created a renewable defense in principle, but the inexperienced pairs still have to master flight and discover how dragons can destroy Thread without relying on the colony's dwindling aircraft.

The first dragons and riders learn to fight as a unit. Firestone lets the dragons produce flame, and their ability to move through the cold emptiness called between allows them to cross great distances instantly when given a clear destination. These abilities turn them from a genetic possibility into Pern's best long-term defense. At the same time, the settlement's unity is threatened by people who still hope to recover an interstellar escape. Avril Bitra uses her piloting skills and access to the old ships in pursuit of her own departure, forcing the colony's loyal pilots to act before the remaining orbital resources are taken beyond the settlers' reach.

Avril's attempt to seize a route away from Pern ends in space. Sallah Telgar prevents the theft but dies in the effort, closing off the fantasy that the settlement can simply reverse its founding choice. On the ground, environmental danger and the decline of irreplaceable machinery force a final move away from Landing. The colonists carry north what people, animals, records, and equipment they can save. Sorka and Faranth, Sean and Carenath, and the other dragon pairs have proved they can flame Thread and travel between, so their breeding population can replace the temporary aerial defenses. The riders occupy the vast caverns above the new settlement at Fort, with Sean and Sorka as their central leaders. This first Weyr, together with the developing Holds and crafts, establishes the social order by which later generations will survive the Passes of Thread.

characters.description: A fisherman's daughter from a remote coastal hold, newly brought to the Harper Hall as the Masterharper's own apprentice. She plays every instrument in the hall, writes songs already being sung across Pern, and is bonded to nine fire lizards, the first person known to have Impressed them deliberately. She is also the first girl the Hall has taken as an apprentice, arrives with a badly scarred hand, no craft training, no idea what she is entitled to, and a settled conviction from her upbringing that she is a nuisance who will shortly be sent home.
characters.name: Menolly

characters.description: The Masterharper of Pern, head of a craft whose halls and posted harpers reach every hold on the planet, which makes him both Pern's teacher and its best-informed politician. Genial, hard to mislead and given to arranging things several steps ahead, he brought Menolly to the Hall himself and has not explained to her, or to most of his craftmasters, exactly why.
characters.name: Robinton

characters.description: The gold queen of Menolly's nine fire lizards and the leader of her clutch: small, brilliantly possessive and unwilling to be more than a few feet from her. The other eight take their cue from her, which means Menolly's moods arrive in a room before she does.
characters.name: Beauty

characters.description: Headwoman of the Harper Hall, who runs its kitchens, stores, laundry and lodgings and knows more about its people than any of the craftmasters. Warm and briskly sensible, she is the first person at the Hall to work out that the new apprentice has arrived with nothing and expects less.
characters.name: Silvina

characters.description: A large, simple-minded man who carries and scrubs in the Harper Hall kitchens under Silvina's eye. Slow of speech and easily confused, he is entirely captivated by the fire lizards and becomes devoted to the business of feeding them.
characters.name: Camo

characters.description: The woman who keeps the cottage where the Hall's girl students are lodged. Anxious about her own standing and about the well-connected families whose daughters she houses, she resents having an apprentice, a fisherman's daughter and nine fire lizards imposed on her.
characters.name: Dunca

characters.description: A young apprentice with a celebrated treble voice, an unerring instinct for what is going on anywhere in the Hall, and a habit of trading information for advantage. Cheerful and quite unimpressed by rank, he attaches himself to Menolly early and explains the Hall's politics to her whether or not she asks.
characters.name: Piemur

characters.description: A journeyman harper who works closely with the Masterharper and travels on his errands. Quiet, observant and easy to underestimate, he is one of the few people at the Hall who treats Menolly as a colleague from the start.
characters.name: Sebell

characters.description: The granddaughter of a Lord Holder, lodged in the same cottage as Menolly to be taught the accomplishments expected of a hold's daughter. Conscious of her family's standing and quick to organize the other girls, she takes the arrival of a sea hold's daughter with an apprentice's status as an insult.
characters.name: Pona

characters.description: The Harper Hall's master of composition: exacting, sardonic and openly sceptical that the Masterharper's new apprentice is anything but a fashionable acquisition. He sets Menolly work designed to find the limits of what she can actually do.
characters.name: Domick

characters.description: The Hall's voice master, an enormous man who teaches by bellowing and who cares about nothing except whether a singer is producing the sound properly. He takes Menolly's training in hand without any reference to the argument going on around her.
characters.name: Shonagar

characters.description: The craftmaster in charge of making instruments, absorbed in wood, glue and tuning to the exclusion of Hall politics. He judges people by what their hands produce, which turns out to be a fairer test than Menolly expects.
characters.name: Jerint

characters.description: An elderly craftmaster who teaches musical theory and the strict forms, and who regards the notion of a girl apprenticed to the Harper Craft as an affront to the way things are done. He examines Menolly with the clear intention of finding her wanting.
characters.name: Morshal

characters.description: One of the girls lodged at the cottage, less certain than the rest that the newcomer deserves what is being done to her. She is genuinely interested in music rather than in accomplishments, which puts her at odds with the others.
characters.name: Audiva

characters.description: Masterhealer of Pern, based near the Harper Hall: a small, stooped, extremely capable man who is the first person to look properly at the scar across Menolly's palm and to say what can be done about it. He is blunt about what her family's treatment of the wound cost her.
characters.name: Oldive

characters.description: Lord Holder of Fort Hold, the largest hold on Pern and the Harper Hall's neighbour: loud, choleric, conventional in his views about women and crafts, and determined to have a fire lizard of his own now that he knows they can be Impressed.
characters.name: Lord Groghe

recaps.ending: Menolly's standing at the Harper Hall is settled in her favour on every count. Her hand, treated properly by Masterhealer Oldive and worked steadily, recovers enough for her to play as she used to. The craftmasters who set out to test her, Domick and Morshal in particular, are satisfied by what she can actually do: she sight-reads and performs Domick's demanding new work and holds her own in theory, instrument-making and voice. The trouble at the girls' cottage ends with her out of it and lodged in the Hall itself, and Pona's clique loses its ground. Fire lizards spread further under her instruction, including a queen for Lord Groghe of Fort Hold, and Menolly's own songs are being sung across Pern by harpers who have no idea who wrote them. At the Hall's evening meal the Masterharper ends her apprenticeship after a matter of days and walks her to the journeymen's tables, making her a journeywoman of the Harper Craft, the first woman to hold the rank. Her fear that she was brought to the Hall only as the keeper of nine fire lizards is put to rest: she was brought there to write. What is not settled is what the Masterharper actually intends to do with a journeywoman whose songs travel faster than his harpers do.
recaps.in_short: Menolly arrives at the Harper Hall as the Masterharper's apprentice, the first girl the craft has taken, with nine fire lizards, a scarred hand and no idea what she is entitled to. Lodged among Lord Holders' daughters who resent her, tested by craftmasters who assume she is a fashionable indulgence, and convinced she was brought only because of her fire lizards, she works through a punishing few days of examinations in composition, theory, voice and instrument-making. Master Oldive treats her hand so that it will heal properly; Silvina, the apprentice Piemur, the journeyman Sebell and the kitchen helper Camo take her side; the bullying at the girls' cottage comes to a head and she is moved into the Hall itself. She teaches others to Impress fire lizards, including the Lord of Fort Hold, and she discovers that songs she wrote alone on a beach are already being sung across Pern. At the end of the week the Masterharper ends her apprenticeship and walks her to the journeymen's tables, making her the Harper Craft's first journeywoman.

recaps.text: Pern's people shelter in stone holds from Thread, a spore that falls from a neighbouring planet and devours anything living; dragons and their bonded riders burn it out of the sky, and the crafts, each with its own hall and Master, supply everything else. The Harper Craft reaches furthest of all: harpers are posted to every hold, and their teaching ballads carry Pern's history, law and survival lore, so the Masterharper's word travels everywhere. In Dragonsong, Menolly, youngest child of the Sea Holder at the remote Half-Circle Sea Hold, was taught music in secret by the hold's old harper Petiron, who sent two of her songs to the Masterharper without saying whose they were. When Petiron died her family forbade her music, insisting a girl could not be a harper, and a gash across her palm was allowed to heal badly enough to end her playing. She ran away, sheltered in a cliff cave during Threadfall, and was present when a clutch of fire-lizard eggs she had saved from the tide hatched; she Impressed nine of the creatures, which nobody had known was possible. Living wild on the coast worked her scarred hand loose again. Caught in the open during a Fall, she was rescued by a dragonrider and taken to Benden Weyr, where the Masterharper found her, identified her as the author of the two songs, and took her away to the Harper Hall as his apprentice.

Menolly reaches the Harper Hall in Fort with her nine fire lizards and immediately runs into a problem nobody warned her about: the Hall has never had a girl apprentice, so there is nowhere obvious to put her. She is lodged not in the apprentice dormitories but in a cottage where a keeper named Dunca houses girl students, most of them daughters and granddaughters of Lord Holders sent to acquire accomplishments rather than a craft. Their reaction to a fisherman's daughter with an apprentice's knot, the Masterharper's personal attention and nine fire lizards is immediate and hostile, and Pona, the best connected of them, organizes the rest. Menolly, raised to expect exactly this, assumes it is her own fault and keeps her head down. Silvina, the Hall's headwoman, and Camo, a slow-witted kitchen worker enchanted by the fire lizards, are the first people to treat her decently.

Menolly's first days are a succession of examinations, because the craftmasters were given an apprentice without explanation and mean to find out what she is. Master Shonagar takes her voice in hand and cares about nothing else. Master Jerint puts her among the instrument-makers to see what her hands can do. Master Morshal, who considers the whole business improper, tests her theory expecting to find gaps. Master Domick, the composition master, is the most pointed of all, treating her as a fashionable acquisition of the Masterharper's and setting work designed to expose her. Meanwhile the apprentice Piemur, who knows everything happening in the Hall, attaches himself to her and starts explaining the politics, and the journeyman Sebell treats her as a colleague. Masterhealer Oldive examines the scar across her palm and tells her plainly that it was mishandled, that it can be improved, and that she must not play until he says so.

Forbidden to play while her hand is treated, Menolly is left with time, no clear place in the Hall's hierarchy and a growing conviction that the Masterharper brought her only because she can Impress fire lizards. Her clutch is a continuing disruption: they follow her everywhere, respond to her feelings, and fascinate everyone who sees them, which does nothing to reduce the resentment at the cottage. The campaign against her escalates from exclusion to open accusation, with Dunca inclined to believe the girls whose families matter to her. Only Audiva, one of the cottage girls, is uneasy about it. The situation ends with Menolly out of Dunca's cottage and lodged in the Harper Hall itself, which removes her tormentors at a stroke and quietly settles the argument about whether she is a student or an apprentice.

Established in the Hall, Menolly is put to work. She teaches fire-lizard care and Impression to harpers and to visitors, including Lord Groghe of Fort Hold, a conventional and short-tempered man who wants one badly and gets a queen, which converts him from a sceptic into an ally. Sebell, who travels for the Masterharper, wants one for a more practical reason: fire lizards carry messages. Piemur, meanwhile, makes sure she hears about herself, and she discovers that songs she made up alone on a beach with nobody to hear them are being sung all over Pern by harpers who have no idea who wrote them. Domick keeps setting her harder work and keeps getting it back completed, which changes his opinion faster than he admits.

Menolly's hand improves under Oldive's treatment and steady use, and she begins playing again. Domick brings out a demanding new composition of his own and puts her in it, which is both a test and an admission, and she gets through the rehearsals and the performance. Her own songs are performed at the Hall. The craftmasters who examined her have their answers, and the Hall's apprentices, who had been taking their lead from the older students, come round once it becomes clear what she can actually do. What remains unresolved for Menolly is her own fear, which she has not said aloud to anyone: that the fire lizards are the whole reason she is there, and that when the novelty passes she will be sent back to the coast.

The last of the tests are behind her and the Hall's opinion has turned. Morshal's objections are overruled by demonstration, Domick states his verdict in the only way he knows how, and Robinton, who has been letting the craftmasters reach their own conclusions rather than imposing his, judges the argument finished. Menolly is teaching, composing and playing again, with Silvina, Sebell, Piemur, Camo and Audiva around her and no cottage to go back to. She is still expecting to be told her place is provisional.

At the Hall's evening meal the Masterharper ends Menolly's apprenticeship after barely a sevenday and walks her to the journeymen's tables, making her a journeywoman of the Harper Craft and the first woman to hold the rank. The craftmasters who spent the week testing her, Domick and Morshal included, accept the judgement because they made it themselves. Her hand is healing, her songs are already travelling Pern ahead of her, the fire lizards are being Impressed all over the north with her as the authority on how, and Lord Groghe of Fort is an ally rather than an obstacle. Her fear that she had been taken in only as the keeper of nine fire lizards is answered directly: she was brought to the Hall because of what she writes. She ends the book with a craft, a rank, a place to live and the Masterharper's plans for her still unexplained.

characters.description: A fugitive wizard left nearly blind and badly depleted after sealing a portal. Still pursued by a hostile organization, he remains near the breach with his injured companions to find a dragon that escaped from the Nether.
characters.name: Kazimir Wolfe

characters.description: Kazimir's talking dog and devoted companion. He guides Kazimir away from the portal site when the wizard can barely see, combining unusual speech and understanding with the instincts, loyalties, and distractions of an ordinary dog.
characters.name: Duke

characters.description: A jinn from the Nether who serves as Kazimir's reluctant magical adviser. He is initially dormant after giving Kazimir his available power during the portal fight, leaving his intentions and the cost of that aid uncertain.
characters.name: Azib

characters.description: An agent allied with Kazimir and the field organizer of the escape from the breach. Injured alongside the rest of the group, he manages concealment, transport, and the practical search for the escaped dragon.
characters.name: Mike

characters.description: An allied field agent wounded in the portal-site fight. She joins the injured party's extraction of Kazimir and Duke, then helps the group evade pursuit and conceal its trail.
characters.name: Isabel

characters.description: An injured ancient knight who drives the fleeing group after the portal fight.
characters.name: Macarius

characters.description: A time-displaced warrior injured during the escape from the portal site. Her damaged ankle limits her movement while she adapts to modern concealment, supported by another agent and protected by Macarius as a fellow knight.
characters.name: Giselle

characters.description: An aged, speaking three-toed feline from the Nether, found injured in a trap. After Kazimir offers rescue instead of death, he makes a binding pledge not to harm Kazimir's household and to protect its members when he can.
characters.name: Nether feline

characters.description: The remote leader who receives an agent's reports about the widening crisis. She is briefed about the rescued Nether feline and the two flying creatures still at large, serving as the field team's off-site decision-maker.
characters.name: Annie

characters.description: An armored, sword-bearing man encountered by a sheriff's deputy at the mound. He asks for a wizard, withstands a taser, attacks the deputy, and escapes into the woods.
characters.name: Armored knight

characters.description: The smaller of two winged creatures that emerge from the Nether. Still young, it has not yet developed the ability to breathe fire.
characters.name: Young dragon

characters.description: A winged Nether creature identified by its separate trail near the sealed breach. At roughly ten to twelve feet long, it is larger than the young dragon that escaped alongside it.
characters.name: Wyvern

characters.description: A federal agent who already knows that magic exists and does not accept that Kazimir committed two earlier killings. Kazimir considers asking her to risk covert access to police evidence that may help locate the escaped creatures.
characters.name: Michelle Singer

characters.description: A confused, armed man reported near the breach who identifies himself only as being from a distant region and asks for a wizard. His unfamiliarity with the present suggests another displaced knight, but his identity and purpose remain unconfirmed.
characters.name: Armed stranger

characters.description: A homeowner caught in the path of the armed stranger. The intruder holds him at swordpoint, demands the location of a wizard, and reacts violently to modern technology before fleeing with supplies.
characters.name: Paul Delage

characters.description: An overseas reinforcement agent travelling with a partner to assist Mike and Isabel. Concealed shooters ambush the pair at a gas station before they reach the group.
characters.name: Rosa

characters.description: An overseas reinforcement agent travelling with a partner to assist the field operation. He uses a cover identity like the other agents and is shot when hidden attackers intercept the pair at a gas station.
characters.name: Carlos

characters.description: A technology-focused civilian investigator drawn to the supposed dinosaur sighting. He arrives with analytical equipment, photographs, and ash-like material recovered from the earlier collision, though none of it yet provides conclusive public proof.
characters.name: Mario

characters.description: A civilian conspiracy hunter who joins the growing search with film cameras and motion-sensitive gear. His use of physical negatives makes him a particular concern for a group trying to keep authentic images of the dragon from public view.
characters.name: Clint

characters.description: An elder god of the Nether whose presence lies beyond Kazimir's newly opened portal. Vastly powerful and hostile, he seizes the wizard's will and tries to force the passage to remain open so he can enter this world.
characters.name: Apophis

characters.description: Kazimir's deceased guardian and first teacher in minor magical practices. She raised and trained him before armed attackers killed her, while the truth about her relationship to him and her part in his parents' deaths remained unresolved.
characters.name: Deceased guardian

characters.description: An ancient wizard spirit sharing Duke's body while remaining distinct from the dog. Drawn to Kazimir to train him, the spirit cannot be separated from Duke, and its earlier relationship with Azib remains unexplained.
characters.name: Ancient wizard spirit

recaps.ending:
Kazimir's false portal signal draws the young dragon to an isolated field, but the same magic intensifies the cold and fog, ruining the planned rifle attack. Kazimir shocks the chaotic energy clinging to the creature, Macarius and Duke stop it from escaping, and Kazimir places it into a magical sleep. The party transports it to the former breach, where Kazimir opens a portal and sends the awakened dragon back to the Nether alive.

An elder Nether god seizes Kazimir's will and forces him to hold the portal open. Kazimir breaks the control by injuring himself until he loses consciousness, closing the passage before the god can enter. The escaped-creature crisis is resolved, but traces of both animals remain vulnerable to public discovery. Kazimir survives with a likely concussion and accepts the Convergence as a world-level threat. Duke, Mike, the injured agent, Macarius, and Giselle remain with him. Azib and the Nether feline decline the chance to return to the Nether, while the remote leader's allied network and the federal contact remain allies under continuing security pressure. Kazimir intends to strike the hostile organization, whose magical archives, compromised operations, and wider plans remain unresolved.
recaps.in_short: After sealing a portal created by a hostile organization, Kazimir Wolfe and his allies discover that a wyvern, a young dragon, and a speaking Nether feline crossed into this world. The wyvern dies in a road collision, while the group follows the dragon to a later search region amid public sightings, enemy attacks, and the arrival of a time-displaced assassin. Kazimir develops new control over chaotic energy and devises a false portal signal to lure the dragon. With Macarius and Duke, he captures it alive and opens a real portal to return it to the Nether. An elder Nether god then takes control of Kazimir and tries to enter through the opening. Kazimir knocks himself unconscious to close the portal. Injured but convinced that the Convergence is real, he resolves to lead an offensive against the hostile organization, while Azib and the Nether feline choose to remain with his group.

recaps.text:
Previously: Kazimir Wolfe's guardian raised him and introduced him to minor magical practices before armed attackers killed her. Her death became one of Kazimir's reasons for opposing a hostile organization, but her true relationship to him and her role in the deaths of his parents remained unresolved.

An ancient wizard spirit was drawn to Kazimir in order to train him. Instead of arriving alone, the spirit became bound to Duke's body and could not be separated from the dog. It remained a distinct presence, while Duke gained speech and unusual understanding without losing his own identity or ordinary canine nature. The spirit's earlier relationship with the jinn Azib was also unresolved.

Kazimir is left temporarily blind and dangerously depleted after sealing the portal. Mike extracts him, Duke, an injured agent, Macarius, and Giselle, but police and a hostile organization are searching the area. Kazimir remains because at least one dragon escaped. Tracks soon establish that both a young dragon and a wyvern crossed from the Nether. A third trail leads to an intelligent, three-toed feline trapped in the woods. Kazimir rescues him, and the feline makes a binding pledge to protect Kazimir's household when able.

The creatures scatter while the injured party hides in a motel. Azib explains that fragments of the hostile organization's ritual bowl may retain chaotic energy capable of tracing them. Police have collected the fragments, so Kazimir considers asking a federal contact for covert access. The feline then develops a severe fever caused by dark energy in his injured leg. Kazimir extracts the energy at considerable risk and saves him, adding a further life debt between them. The federal contact agrees to try arranging private contact with the evidence. Meanwhile, a trail camera records a winged creature attacking a deer decoy, and the video begins spreading online despite being dismissed as a fake.

With help from the federal contact, Kazimir enters police custody under a cover identity and transfers the shattered bowl's remaining energy into a cast-iron pot. Its pulses give the party rough headings for the dragon and wyvern, but the power is fading. A separate report leads the injured agent, Macarius, and Giselle toward an armed man who appears displaced from the year 519. One winged Nether creature is then killed in a truck collision and dissolves, leaving little evidence behind.

The stranger uses magic to draw Kazimir's team into the forest. He claims to seek a wizard and pretends to offer service, then tries to assassinate Kazimir. Duke, Giselle, and Macarius stop him. The captive declares support for a Convergence and the return of old gods before killing himself. Two incoming reinforcement agents are ambushed and killed, and a compromised message exposes Kazimir and the injured agent to another attack. Mike finally identifies their allied network and its long-standing enemy.

The survivors continue east. Their last magical scans place the remaining dragon in a northern lake region, but the pot's tracking energy is exhausted. They establish a rental house and prepare to search by conventional means. The Nether feline chooses to stay with Kazimir and opposes a Convergence that would threaten both worlds.

Thermal drones prove unreliable because Nether creatures may produce little infrared signal. A blurry public video nevertheless confirms that the young dragon is alive in the search region, while the remote leader releases convincing false footage to weaken belief in the real sighting. The dead creature from the earlier collision is therefore identified as the wyvern. At the dragon's latest location, Kazimir learns that he can compress and trigger the chaotic residue attached to it, suggesting a close-range way to disable it.

The dragon ranges too widely for the team's search grid. Two civilian investigators join the growing public hunt, bringing recovered residue, film cameras, and other equipment that could expose the truth. The hostile organization has also exploited allied communications, and the federal contact's inquiry links the attack on the reinforcement agents to hired criminals while leaving their employer unknown.

Kazimir studies the failed Convergence expected by the assassin from 519, but his theory that an earlier wizard prevented it remains unproved. Macarius and Giselle then explain why protectors were sent through time: wizards and their defenders were being hunted, so future wizards near a Convergence were expected to need help. They were told to find the wizard most in need, not given Kazimir's identity or era. Kazimir concludes that the enemy's archives may contain the answers his group lacks.

Repeated drone searches fail as public interest in the dragon grows. Giselle argues that the creature is a displaced animal rather than inherently evil, and Kazimir develops a plan to attract it with magic instead of ordinary bait. Azib believes a false portal signal could tempt a dragon seeking a route home, though such a lure could also expose Kazimir to the hostile organization. The remote leader approves a diversion rather than a direct attack on enemy personnel.

Kazimir's control expands while he treats lingering injuries in the Nether feline. He eases distorted energy in the feline's body, calms his mind, and places him into sleep. The group selects an isolated, screened field for the dragon encounter. The remote leader fabricates a sighting at a diversion site to draw civilian pursuers and enemy units away, while Mike acquires a powerful rifle as a last resort. The preferred plan is for Kazimir to disrupt the chaotic energy clinging to the dragon and then calm it before the agents shoot.

At a remote wildlife refuge, Kazimir learns to reproduce portal-like energy strongly enough for Azib to detect. The effort exhausts him, but the test succeeds. With the deception attracting several enemy teams, the allied network obtains a box truck and commits to the operation that night before worsening weather or fading interest ends the diversion.

Kazimir emits the false portal signal in the isolated field while Mike and the injured agent take firing positions. The magic intensifies the cold and fog, destroying visibility and forcing Mike to cancel the planned shot. The dragon advances through the cover and attacks Kazimir. He shocks its chaotic residue, and Macarius and Duke keep it from flying until Macarius renders it unconscious. Kazimir then places it into a magical sleep, allowing the group to secure it alive in the box truck.

They transport the dragon to the former portal site while Kazimir sustains the sleep. The Nether feline explains that he fled a devastated Nether but remains because he expects Kazimir's future help for his people. He and Azib both decline an offer to return. Despite uncertain alignment, Kazimir opens a portal, and the team drives the awakened, reluctant dragon through it.

As the passage closes, an elder Nether god takes control of Kazimir and forces him to keep it open. Kazimir repeatedly strikes his own head against the truck until unconsciousness breaks the control and closes the portal. The dragon is back in the Nether and Kazimir survives, injured. The encounter confirms the Convergence as an existential threat. He resolves to lead an offensive against the hostile organization while his companions remain together and the motives of their Nether allies remain open.

characters.description: The youngest child of the Sea Holder of Half-Circle Sea Hold, a remote fishing hold on Pern's northern coast. She has been taught music by the hold's old harper and has an unusual gift for it, both as a player of every instrument in the hall and as a maker of her own tunes, which is the part her family finds unforgivable. Half-Circle is a conservative hold where children are useful or they are nothing, and where everyone agrees that a girl cannot be a harper. Quick, capable and used to being corrected, she has learned to keep the thing she cares about most out of sight.
characters.name: Menolly

characters.description: The old harper of Half-Circle Sea Hold, who has taught the hold's children their songs and duties for many Turns and taught Menolly far more than that. Frail and near the end of his life, he is the only person at Half-Circle who values what she can do.
characters.name: Petiron

characters.description: Sea Holder of Half-Circle and Menolly's father: a hard, literal man who judges everything by whether it feeds the hold and mistrusts anything that does not. He regards his daughter's music as an embarrassment now that there is no harper to excuse it, and disciplines her for it without hesitation.
characters.name: Yanus

characters.description: Menolly's mother and the headwoman of Half-Circle, who runs the hold's stores, kitchens and women with brisk efficiency. She has no patience for anything unproductive and expects her daughter to accept the same narrow life she did.
characters.name: Mavi

characters.description: Menolly's older sister, who has settled comfortably into what Half-Circle expects of her and is quick to report her sister's lapses. She resents the attention Menolly's abilities attract.
characters.name: Sella

characters.description: One of Menolly's older brothers, a ship's captain of the hold's fishing fleet. He is the member of her family who is straightforwardly kind to her, appreciates her music without making an issue of it, and notices more about her situation than anyone else at Half-Circle.
characters.name: Alemi

characters.description: The young harper sent from the Harper Hall to replace Half-Circle's old one. Newly walked the tables and eager, he finds the hold's music better drilled than he expected and cannot get a straight answer from anyone about who has been teaching the children.
characters.name: Elgion

characters.description: The gold queen of a clutch of fire lizards, small telepathic cousins of Pern's dragons, who bonds to Menolly at hatching. Tiny, vain and fiercely possessive, she leads the rest of the clutch and will not be parted from the person who fed her first.
characters.name: Beauty

characters.description: Weyrwoman of Benden Weyr and rider of the queen dragon Ramoth, the senior queen of Pern. Formidable, direct and impatient with fuss, she takes an interest in an injured girl brought in from a Fall for reasons of her own.
characters.name: Lessa

characters.description: Weyrleader of Benden and rider of the bronze Mnementh, who leads Pern's dragonriders against Thread. He is used to weighing whatever lands in his Weyr for what it might mean to the whole of Pern.
characters.name: F'lar

characters.description: Headwoman of Benden Weyr's lower caverns, who runs its kitchens, stores and infirmary and looks after everyone who comes into her care. Calm, exact and entirely unshockable.
characters.name: Manora

characters.description: A girl of Benden Weyr, close to Menolly's age, sharp-tongued and possessive of the standing her three fire lizards give her, since nobody else at the Weyr has managed more than one.
characters.name: Mirrim

characters.description: The Masterharper of Pern, head of the craft whose teaching songs and ballads reach every hold on the planet. Genial, watchful and impossible to mislead for long, he has been looking for the author of two songs sent to him from a coastal hold by a harper now dead.
characters.name: Robinton

recaps.ending: Menolly, taken to Benden Weyr after being caught in the open during Threadfall, recovers there with her nine fire lizards, and the Weyr proves to be the first place that finds her useful rather than embarrassing: her hand loosens with work and healing, and her ability with the creatures is exactly what the Weyr wants explained. The Masterharper of Pern, who has been searching since the old harper Petiron's death for the composer of two songs sent to him from Half-Circle, comes to Benden and identifies the songwriter as Menolly. He takes her into the Harper Craft on the spot as his apprentice. Half-Circle Sea Hold, which had assumed her dead, loses any claim on her, and her family's judgement that a girl cannot be a harper is overturned by the Masterharper himself. She leaves for the Harper Hall with Beauty and the rest of her clutch, no longer hiding what she can do. What remains open is whether a Hall full of boys and craftmasters will actually make room for her, and what Pern will make of a girl who has proved that fire lizards can be Impressed by anyone who reaches them at hatching.
recaps.in_short: Menolly, youngest child of the Sea Holder at the isolated Half-Circle Sea Hold, is a gifted musician and songwriter taught in secret by the hold's old harper. When he dies, her family forbids her to play, insisting that no girl can be a harper, and a badly treated gash across her palm seems to end the question permanently. Forbidden her music and with nothing left at the hold, she runs away. Sheltering in a cliff cave from Threadfall, she is present when a clutch of fire-lizard eggs she had rescued from the tide hatches, and she Impresses nine of the little creatures, something no one on Pern had known was possible. She lives wild on the coast, feeding them and exercising her scarred hand back into use, until she is caught in the open during a Fall and rescued by a dragonrider who takes her to Benden Weyr. There her fire lizards make her remarkable rather than shameful, and the Masterharper of Pern, who has been hunting for the author of two songs sent to him from her hold, identifies her and takes her into his craft as an apprentice.

recaps.text: Pern is a world whose people live in stone holds and cliff caves because of Thread, a spore that falls from a neighbouring planet during a fifty-Turn Pass and devours anything living it touches. Ground crews burn what reaches the earth, but the real defence is dragons: telepathic, bonded for life to a single rider from the moment of hatching, flying out of mountain Weyrs to flame Thread from the sky. Between the Weyrs and the holds sit the crafts, each with its own hall and its own Master. The Harper Craft reaches furthest: harpers are posted to every hold, and besides music they carry the teaching ballads that hold Pern's history, law and survival lore, so a harper is teacher, lawman and news-carrier at once, and the Masterharper's word travels everywhere. Pern is some Turns into a Pass, and the dragonriders' standing has been restored by it. This story takes place well away from the Weyrs and their politics, at a small fishing hold on the northern coast, where none of that matters as much as the tides do.

Half-Circle Sea Hold is a remote fishing hold run by Menolly's father, Yanus, on the principle that everything and everyone must earn their keep. Menolly, his youngest, has been taught music by the hold's old harper, Petiron, and is better at it than anyone there realizes: she plays every instrument in the hall and, more dangerously, makes up her own songs. Petiron has quietly sent two of them to the Masterharper without telling anyone whose they are. When Petiron dies, the hold is left without a harper until the Harper Hall can send a replacement, and Menolly is set to teaching the children their ballads in the meantime, on strict condition that she teach only what is written and add nothing of her own. Her parents' view, stated plainly, is that a girl cannot be a harper, and that her tunings are an embarrassment to be stamped out before the new harper arrives.

Menolly is caught playing her own music for the hold's children and punished for it. Set to gutting the catch, she slices her left hand open, and the wound is stitched and bound in a way that leaves the palm scarred and tight; she is told, and comes to believe, that she will never play properly again. The new harper, Elgion, arrives from the Harper Hall to find the hold's children better drilled than any he expected and nobody willing to say who taught them. Menolly is kept away from him, told to say nothing about her music, and given work that keeps her out of the hall. Out gathering along the shore, she comes across a fire lizard, a small wild cousin of the dragons that most of Pern regards as a legend, and finds the clutch of eggs it has laid in the sand where the tide will reach them. She carries the eggs up into a cave in the cliff, above the water line.

With her hand ruined, her music forbidden and her family already arranging the rest of her life, Menolly leaves Half-Circle rather than accept it. She is still out on the coast when Threadfall comes, and shelters in the cliff cave where she put the fire-lizard eggs, running the last stretch ahead of the leading edge of the Fall. She survives, but by then the hold has counted her lost and stopped looking, and she decides not to go back at all. Her plan reaches no further than the cave, a store of salvaged food and firestone, and the eggs warming in the sand at the back of it.

The eggs hatch while Menolly is in the cave with them. Newly hatched fire lizards will eat until they burst or fly off and starve, and she keeps them alive by feeding them from her own supplies as fast as she can cut. Nine of them bond to her in the process, among them a gold queen she names Beauty, and she becomes the first person on Pern to Impress fire lizards deliberately, though she does not know that is what she has done. She lives wild on the coast for some time, hunting and gathering to feed a clutch that never stops being hungry, sleeping rough and moving with the Fall timetable. The constant work of catching, cutting and climbing does what nobody at Half-Circle attempted: it stretches the scar on her hand loose again, and she finds she can use it. She also makes a pipe and starts making songs again, since there is no one left to forbid it.

At Half-Circle, Elgion pieces together that the hold's ballads were taught by someone who has gone, and he and Menolly's brother Alemi begin to suspect what the hold has thrown away, particularly once fire lizards are sighted along the coast. Menolly, out too far from her cave, is caught in the open with a Fall coming down and runs for shelter she cannot reach. A dragonrider on sweep sees her, picks her up, and carries her and her fire lizards away to Benden Weyr, where the healers treat her injuries and Manora, the headwoman of the lower caverns, takes charge of her. The Weyr's reaction to nine fire lizards attending one girl is not the disapproval she expects but intense interest, and the Weyrwoman Lessa wants to know exactly how it was done.

Menolly recovers at Benden Weyr, where she is fed, healed and, for the first time, valued: her fire lizards are the most interesting thing to happen at the Weyr in Turns, and she is set to explaining how to Impress them. She keeps quiet about her music, expecting the same reaction she got at home, and about who she is, expecting to be sent back. Then the Masterharper of Pern arrives at Benden. He has spent Turns trying to trace the composer of two songs sent to him from Half-Circle by the dead harper Petiron, and he identifies Menolly as their author in short order. He takes her into the Harper Craft as his own apprentice and away to the Harper Hall, with Beauty and the rest of her clutch, over any claim her family might make. The girl who was told a girl could not be a harper leaves for the Hall as one.

characters.description: A Miskatonic University student whose interests combine advanced mathematics, physics, and old traditions of magic. He rents an attic room in Arkham's notorious Witch House because its strange angles and history seem relevant to his theories about movement beyond ordinary space.
characters.name: Walter Gilman

characters.description: An accused witch who occupied the house in the seventeenth century. Before vanishing from jail, she reportedly drew baffling curves and angles for her interrogators. Local tradition claims that she and her familiar still return to the attic room.
characters.name: Keziah Mason

characters.description: Keziah Mason's legendary familiar, described in Arkham tales as a ratlike creature with disturbingly human features and tiny hands. Residents of the Witch House blame sounds inside the walls on it, while Gilman's feverish perceptions make the old stories feel immediate.
characters.name: Brown Jenkin

characters.description: Gilman's fellow student and roommate in the Witch House. He notices Gilman's worsening sleep, fever, and unexplained nighttime behavior, and becomes an important witness to the effects of the room upon him.
characters.name: Frank Elwood

characters.description: A professor of mathematics at Miskatonic University. Gilman brings him increasingly radical ideas about dimensions and unusual geometries, leaving Upham concerned by both the substance of the work and his student's declining health.
characters.name: Professor Upham

characters.description: A religious loom fixer who lives in the Witch House and takes its supernatural reputation seriously. Disturbed by what he hears and observes around Gilman, he offers warnings and a protective crucifix.
characters.name: Joe Mazurewicz

characters.description: A dark, imposing figure who appears in Gilman's otherworldly experiences alongside Keziah Mason and demands a formal pledge. He presents himself as an authority within the forces the witch serves.
characters.name: The Black Man

recaps.ending: During the May Eve rite, Gilman resists Keziah and strangles her with the chain of Mazurewicz's crucifix, but Brown Jenkin kills the kidnapped child before escaping. Gilman returns to his room physically shaken and unable to prove the full experience. Soon afterward, Brown Jenkin attacks him in bed and burrows through his body, killing him while Elwood and the other residents hear the struggle. The Witch House is eventually abandoned and later damaged by a storm. When it is demolished, workers discover Keziah's bones, the remains of many sacrificed children, occult objects, and the skeleton of a creature whose anatomy matches the legends of Brown Jenkin. Those findings confirm that material evidence lay behind at least part of Gilman's supposedly fevered experiences, even though the dimensional reaches he witnessed remain beyond ordinary explanation.
recaps.in_short: Miskatonic University student Walter Gilman rents an attic in Arkham's Witch House, hoping its abnormal geometry will support his theories about dimensions. Fever dreams carry him through angular voids while the long-vanished witch Keziah Mason and her ratlike familiar Brown Jenkin draw closer. Physical marks and an object brought back from another world convince him that the journeys are not merely dreams. Keziah and a figure called the Black Man force him toward a supernatural pact and prepare him for a May Eve child sacrifice. Protected by a crucifix, Gilman fights back and kills Keziah, but Brown Jenkin murders the child and escapes. Days later the familiar kills Gilman by tearing through his body. When the decaying house is finally demolished, workers find Keziah's remains, evidence of numerous child sacrifices, occult objects, and Brown Jenkin's inhuman skeleton, confirming the physical core of the horrors Gilman experienced.

recaps.text: Walter Gilman, a gifted Miskatonic University student, studies mathematics and physics alongside Arkham's occult traditions. He deliberately rents the oddly angled attic room once occupied by Keziah Mason, an accused witch who vanished from jail in 1692 after drawing inexplicable geometrical figures. The house is also linked to Brown Jenkin, her ratlike familiar. Gilman believes that the right mathematical understanding could permit travel beyond the familiar three dimensions. Living in the room coincides with fever, sleepwalking, and dreams of moving through a limitless region defined by alien shapes and colors. His roommate Frank Elwood and his professor Upham become concerned, while sounds inside the walls echo the local stories. Gilman begins to perceive Keziah and Brown Jenkin within the dreams, making it harder to dismiss them as products of illness.

Walter Gilman rents the former room of the vanished witch Keziah Mason because its abnormal geometry seems connected to his theories of higher dimensions. Feverish dreams carry him through angular spaces, and the figures of Keziah and her ratlike familiar Brown Jenkin become increasingly distinct. The experiences begin leaving physical traces, including wounds and unexplained mud. In one journey he reaches an alien landscape inhabited by strange life and later finds that he has brought a small manufactured object back to Arkham. Professor Upham cannot identify its material, strengthening Gilman's fear that his mathematical speculations have become actual travel. Elwood watches his health deteriorate, while Joe Mazurewicz, another resident, interprets the nighttime sounds and Gilman's condition through the house's religious and supernatural lore.

Gilman's experiments and fever dreams in the Witch House turn into physical journeys, one of which leaves him with an object from an alien world. Keziah Mason and Brown Jenkin take him through dimensional passages to the presence of a commanding figure called the Black Man, who tries to bind him by having him sign a book. As May Eve approaches, Mazurewicz gives Gilman a crucifix and warns him of imminent danger. Gilman is drawn into a ritual involving a kidnapped child. He finally resists: the crucifix disrupts Keziah, and he strangles the witch with its chain. Brown Jenkin nevertheless attacks the child and completes the killing before escaping. Gilman returns from the ordeal alive, but the disappearance and death associated with the ritual leave him unable to treat what happened as a dream.

Walter Gilman's attempt to use the Witch House's angles for dimensional research entangles him with Keziah Mason, Brown Jenkin, and the Black Man. Though Gilman kills Keziah during a May Eve rite, Brown Jenkin murders the abducted child and escapes. Soon afterward, the familiar enters Gilman's room and kills him by burrowing through his body while Elwood and other tenants hear the attack. The house declines, is abandoned, and is eventually opened during demolition after storm damage. Workers find Keziah's skeleton, the bones of many children, ritual objects, and the remains of a rat-sized being with partly human anatomy. Brown Jenkin's skeleton matches the old descriptions closely enough to validate the house's legends and the immediate cause of Gilman's death. The discoveries do not explain the other worlds or geometrical passages, but they show that his experiences were not only fever dreams.

characters.description: A Martian engineer with a talent for propulsion and a private yacht he has been modifying in his own time. Comfortable, married, and not especially ambitious in a public sense, he has been refining a fusion drive design because the problem interests him rather than because anyone commissioned it, and he intends to take the result out for a quiet test flight himself.
characters.name: Solomon Epstein

characters.description: Solomon's wife, from a well-established Martian family. She is clear-eyed about her husband's preoccupation with his engineering and about what their life together is, and she is the person he thinks about when he has time to think about anything.
characters.name: Caitlin

recaps.ending: The test works far past anything Solomon predicted. The drive lights and does not stop, the acceleration climbs beyond what a body can take, and the couch he is pinned to becomes the whole of his world. His controls are out of reach, there is no cutoff he can get to, and the drugs and the ship's systems cannot compensate for a burn that simply continues. He works out what he has built while he is dying of it: a drive efficient enough to make the entire solar system reachable, to put Mars in a position to become a real power, and to change what human beings are capable of doing off-planet. He also works out that he will not be there for any of it, and that Caitlin will hear about it after the fact. He dies under acceleration. The yacht keeps burning, carrying his body out of the solar system on a course nothing will ever intercept, and it is still going. The design survives him because the data went out before he did, and the drive that bears his name becomes the foundation of everything the novels take for granted: cheap, fast travel between the planets, a settled Belt, and a Mars strong enough to leave Earth.
recaps.in_short: Solomon Epstein, a Martian engineer, has spent his spare time modifying the fusion drive on his private yacht, and he takes it out alone for a test. It works far better than he expected and then does not stop. The ship accelerates past the limits of what a human body can survive, and with his controls out of reach and no way to shut the burn down, Solomon is pinned to his couch while the drive runs. In the time he has left he understands what he has done: he has built the engine that will make the whole solar system reachable, transform Mars into a genuine power, and open the outer planets to settlement. He also understands that he will not survive it and that his wife Caitlin will learn about it as news. He dies under acceleration, and the yacht carries his body out of the solar system, still burning. The design survives because the data was already transmitted, and the Epstein Drive becomes the technology the entire series rests on.

recaps.text: This is a short prequel and stands entirely alone. It is set roughly a century and a half before the first novel, on a Mars that is an ambitious colony rather than an independent power, at a time when travel between planets is slow, expensive and rare, the outer solar system is effectively unreachable, and Earth is the only serious authority in human affairs. Everything the novels treat as ordinary, ships that cross the system in weeks, a populated asteroid belt, a Mars able to face Earth as an equal, follows from a single piece of engineering. This story is about the man who built it and the flight on which he tested it. No knowledge of the series is required, and nothing about the novels' plots is given away.

Solomon Epstein, a Martian engineer, has been quietly reworking the fusion drive on his own yacht, and he goes up alone to test it, expecting a measurable improvement. What he gets is a drive that is efficient beyond any reasonable projection and that will not shut down. The acceleration climbs past what a person can survive, his controls end up out of reach, and there is no cutoff he can get to; the ship keeps burning with him pinned in the couch. Interleaved with the flight is his ordinary life: the marriage to Caitlin, the work, the reasons he was building the thing at all. Dying, he understands exactly what he has made. The drive will put the entire solar system within reach, give Mars the means to become a power in its own right, and open the outer planets to settlement. He does not survive it. The yacht carries his body out of the solar system, still under thrust, and is still going. The design outlives him because his data was transmitted before the test, and the Epstein Drive becomes the foundation of everything the series is built on.

characters.description: An eighteenth-century surgeon by necessity and a twentieth-century one by training, newly landed in the American colonies with nothing but her instruments and her husband. She is in her early fifties, blunt, and practised at making do, and she knows more than anyone alive about what is coming to this country in the next ten years.
characters.name: Claire Fraser

characters.description: A Highland laird with no land, shipwrecked into the colonies and unwilling to go back to Scotland, where he is still a pardoned traitor with nothing to return to. Tall, red-haired, and used to holding other people's lives together, he is looking for somewhere his family can settle without swearing to anything he cannot keep.
characters.name: Jamie Fraser

characters.description: Jamie's teenaged nephew, long and loose-limbed, who has already survived kidnap and shipwreck and has no intention of being sent home to his mother in Scotland. Cheerful, curious, and reckless, he goes everywhere with his enormous half-wolf dog.
characters.name: Young Ian

characters.description: The French orphan Jamie raised, now a married man with one hand and a great deal of nerve, making a life for himself and his wife in the colonies. Quick-witted and worldly, he handles negotiations that need charm more than force.
characters.name: Fergus Fraser

characters.description: A one-armed Highlander who served years alongside Jamie at Ardsmuir prison and was transported to the colonies afterward. Quiet, self-effacing, and steady, he attaches himself to the Frasers as a friend with nowhere else to be.
characters.name: Duncan Innes

characters.description: Young Ian's dog, a huge animal that is largely wolf, devoted to Ian and alarming to everyone else. He hunts, guards, and repeatedly proves the most useful member of any party he travels with.
characters.name: Rollo

characters.description: An Irish adventurer awaiting execution in Charleston who talks his way into the Frasers' help and escapes the gallows. Handsome, well-spoken, and entirely without conscience, he treats other people as things that can be spent, and he does not forget where his luck came from.
characters.name: Stephen Bonnet

characters.description: Jamie's aunt, sister of the MacKenzie lairds he grew up under, a widow who has made herself one of the richest planters on the Cape Fear river. She is blind, formidable, and used to arranging other people's lives, and she has decided what part her Scottish nephew is going to play in hers.
characters.name: Jocasta Cameron

characters.description: The butler of River Run, an educated and highly capable enslaved man who runs the household and serves as his mistress's eyes, secretary, and memory. Impeccably composed in public, he holds a position of great responsibility and no freedom.
characters.name: Ulysses

characters.description: A vast, hairy, good-natured mountain man who lives easily among both settlers and the Cherokee and guides the Frasers into the back country. Frank about his own anatomy and everyone else's, he is a walking introduction to the people of the mountains.
characters.name: John Quincy Myers

characters.description: An elderly Tuscarora healer and dreamer who recognises Claire as a fellow practitioner and something more, and who trades knowledge of the mountain plants with her. She speaks of Claire in terms Claire does not understand, and gives her a token to keep.
characters.name: Nayawenne

characters.description: Claire's daughter, an engineering student in Boston in 1969, tall and red-haired and as stubborn as both her parents. She has let her mother go and is trying to build an ordinary life, complicated by her attachment to a Scottish historian who keeps disappearing back into the archives.
characters.name: Brianna Randall

characters.description: The Oxford historian who helped Claire find Jamie, now teaching in Scotland and, in his own time, still combing colonial records for traces of the Frasers. Careful and protective by instinct, he is in love with Brianna and unsure what to do about what he keeps finding.
characters.name: Roger Wakefield

characters.description: A tiny, frightened Scottish bondservant girl of about fourteen, taken on as Brianna's maid for the crossing. Fiercely loyal to her mistress and prone to seasickness, fever and misreading situations, she takes it on herself to protect Brianna from what she believes she has understood.
characters.name: Lizzie Wemyss

characters.description: An English nobleman and old friend of Jamie's from his prison years, now a Virginia planter and a widower raising his stepson. Courteous, worldly, and discreet about the obligations that bind him to the Fraser family, he turns up when the family is in difficulty and is willing to spend his own name to help.
characters.name: Lord John Grey

recaps.ending: Jamie, Claire and Young Ian follow Roger north into Iroquois country and find him held in a Mohawk village. Jamie's attempts to buy him back fail, and in the end Young Ian offers himself in Roger's place, is adopted into the village, and stays behind; the parting is permanent as far as any of them know. Roger, who has had months to decide whether he wants a wife carrying a child that may be another man's, chooses to come back. He returns to Fraser's Ridge, where Brianna has borne a son she names Jeremiah, called Jemmy, and accepts the boy as his own without needing to know whose he is. Brianna and Roger are married. Nobody can say whether the child's father is Roger or Stephen Bonnet, and Bonnet himself is still alive and free somewhere in the colonies, with Claire's stolen ring and a grudge. Claire and Jamie remain on the Ridge, holding a newspaper notice from a future decade that reports their own deaths in a house fire, and beginning to build something that they know history says will burn.
recaps.in_short: Shipwrecked into the American colonies, Jamie and Claire refuse a rich inheritance from Jamie's aunt at her slave-worked plantation and take a land grant in the North Carolina mountains instead, founding Fraser's Ridge. In 1969, Roger finds a newspaper notice recording that James and Claire Fraser died in a fire on that Ridge in 1776, and hides it from Brianna. She finds it herself, follows her mother through the standing stones to warn them, and Roger goes after her. In Wilmington the two quarrel and part after handfasting; that same night Brianna is raped by Stephen Bonnet, a pirate the Frasers once helped escape hanging. Arriving pregnant at the Ridge, she cannot say whose the child is. Her young maid misidentifies Roger as the man who attacked her, and Jamie beats him and lets Young Ian sell him to the Mohawk. When the mistake comes to light, Jamie and Claire go north to buy him back, and Ian trades himself for Roger's freedom. Roger returns, claims Brianna's newborn son as his own, and the two are married.

recaps.text: Previously, in the Outlander books: Claire Randall travelled from 1945 to 1743 through the standing stones at Craigh na Dun, married the Highlander Jamie Fraser, and failed with him to prevent the Jacobite rising. On the eve of Culloden he sent her back to her own century pregnant, expecting to die in the battle; Claire returned to her first husband, Frank Randall, who raised their daughter Brianna as his own, and became a surgeon in Boston. Twenty years later, after Frank's death, Claire told Brianna the truth, and the historian Roger Wakefield found proof that Jamie had survived Culloden. Jamie in fact lived through the battle, hid for years as an outlaw, spent more years in Ardsmuir prison, and fathered a son he cannot acknowledge while paroled to an English estate. Claire went back through the stones and found him in Edinburgh, a printer and smuggler, and had to work through a marriage he had made in her absence. Chasing his kidnapped nephew Young Ian to the West Indies, the family confronted Geillis Duncan, another traveller, whom Claire killed; a hurricane then wrecked their ship and cast them ashore on the coast of Georgia, in the American colonies.

In 1767 the Frasers are in Charleston, without money or land, watching an old friend from Jamie's prison years hang for theft. At the gaol they meet another condemned man, an Irishman named Stephen Bonnet, and help him get free of his irons and out of the city, largely because Jamie will not leave a man to hang if he can prevent it. The party, Jamie, Claire, Young Ian, Fergus, Duncan Innes and the dog Rollo, travels inland by river toward Cross Creek and Jamie's aunt. On the water they are boarded at night by river pirates led by Bonnet, who robs them of the gemstones that are all their capital and takes Claire's wedding ring from her first husband. Claire manages to keep Jamie's ring hidden. They arrive at River Run with nothing.

River Run is a large, prosperous plantation on the Cape Fear, run by Jamie's blind aunt Jocasta Cameron with the help of her butler Ulysses and worked by a great many enslaved people. Jocasta is delighted by her nephew and quickly makes plain what she intends: to name Jamie her heir and settle the estate on him. Jamie refuses. He will not own people, and North Carolina law makes freeing them nearly impossible, so accepting the inheritance would trap him. A violent incident on the estate shows exactly how the colony's law treats an enslaved man accused of harming a white overseer, and hardens the decision. Duncan Innes takes a place in Jocasta's household. Looking for another way to settle, Jamie is offered a large land grant in the western mountains by the royal governor, on terms that require him to bring in settlers and, eventually, to answer if the Crown calls.

Guided by the mountain man John Quincy Myers, the Frasers ride west into the back country, well beyond the settled lands and into territory claimed by the Cherokee. Jamie chooses a site on a wooded ridge with good water and a view over the valley, and names it Fraser's Ridge. He negotiates carefully with the Cherokee to make it clear that they are neighbours rather than invaders. Claire begins gathering the mountain plants she will need and finds a practice waiting for her among the scattered settlers and the native villages. It is a beautiful, empty, dangerous place, and everything they will have has to be built from nothing before winter.

The first year on the Ridge is spent felling timber, raising a cabin, laying in food, and learning what the mountain can and cannot provide. Jamie kills a bear at close quarters and earns a name and a reputation among the Cherokee for it. Young Ian takes to the country completely, spending as much time with the native hunters as with his uncle. Claire meets an elderly Tuscarora healer, Nayawenne, who trades plant knowledge with her, treats her as something more than a fellow physician, and gives her a stone to keep. Settlers begin to trickle in. The Frasers are poor, isolated and entirely occupied with surviving, and for the first time in years they have somewhere that is theirs.

In 1969 and 1970, Brianna is studying in Boston and Roger is teaching in Scotland, seeing each other when they can and quarrelling about how much Roger wants to settle things. Roger has never stopped searching colonial records for the Frasers, and he finds a newspaper notice reporting that James Fraser and his wife died in a fire that destroyed their house on Fraser's Ridge. He hides it, unwilling to hand Brianna her mother's death. Brianna finds it anyway. Furious with him for concealing it, and certain that she can reach her parents in time to warn them, she resolves to follow her mother back.

Brianna goes to Scotland, prepares as her mother did, and passes through the standing stones at Craigh na Dun. Roger learns what she has done and follows, working his passage to the colonies as a crewman aboard a ship whose captain turns out to be Stephen Bonnet; he sees Bonnet drown surplus passengers for profit and understands exactly what kind of man is loose in the country. Brianna lands and makes her way toward Wilmington, accompanied by Lizzie, a small Scottish bondservant girl whose indenture she has taken over. Roger tracks her down there. Their reunion turns into a quarrel when she learns he had hidden the death notice from her, but they make it up, agree to a handfast marriage, and spend the night together. Roger then leaves to settle his affairs and secure a way home for them both, intending to return within weeks; Brianna, who does not know when to expect him, is left in Wilmington alone.

Stephen Bonnet is in Wilmington, and he still has the ring he took from Claire on the river. Brianna, trying to get her mother's ring back from him, is caught alone by Bonnet and raped. She tells no one what has happened, gathers Lizzie, and continues upriver to River Run and then into the mountains to find her parents, carrying the warning she crossed two centuries to deliver.

Brianna reaches Fraser's Ridge and meets her father for the first time. The reunion is overwhelming for all three of them, and it is quickly overtaken by two facts: the newspaper notice that says her parents will die in a fire, and Brianna's pregnancy. She tells Claire she was raped and cannot know whether the child is Roger's or Bonnet's. Lizzie, who saw only that her mistress was ruined by a man and then saw Roger arrive asking for Brianna, tells Jamie that this is the man. Jamie and Young Ian beat Roger nearly to death without letting him speak, and Ian, thinking he is sparing his uncle a hanging, sells him to a band of Mohawk traders passing through, who take him north.

The mistake comes out when Brianna hears Roger's name and description, and the family has to face what they have done. Jamie sets off north with Claire and Young Ian to find the Mohawk village and buy Roger back, carrying what little the family can raise in trade goods. Brianna, too far along to travel, waits at River Run under Jocasta's roof, where Lord John Grey, an old friend of her father's, comes to keep an eye on her and eventually offers to marry her so that the child will have a name and protection. She bears a son. Stephen Bonnet is still at large, and the question of the baby's father is one nobody can answer.

The search ends at a Mohawk village far to the north, where Roger has been kept as a captive and has survived a brutal ordeal at the hands of the village. Jamie's offers are refused, and the standoff is broken only when Young Ian offers himself in Roger's place. The Mohawk accept, adopt Ian into the village, and let Roger go; his family leaves him there, with no expectation of seeing him again. Roger, who has spent months deciding whether he can accept a wife and a child who may be Bonnet's, chooses to come back. He arrives at Fraser's Ridge, meets Brianna's newborn son, and claims the boy as his own without asking whose he is. Brianna names the child Jeremiah, called Jemmy, and she and Roger are married. Bonnet remains alive and free, and Claire and Jamie go on building a settlement they have been told in print will one day burn with them in it.
